p01.why: Base with an argument list names the template, so the two inherited injected names are not ambiguous here.

p02.why: Array-to-pointer, function-to-pointer, qualification, dropping noexcept and nullptr are all allowed conversions.

p03.why: A qualified name that finds a template opens an argument list.

p04.why: Equal enumerator values, unions with the same active member and value, and equal array members name the same specialization.

p05.why: Explicit arguments fill R and T, U takes its default long, and 1.5 converts to 1.

p06.why: The definition's head gives C no default, so C<> has too few arguments.

p07.why: A pointer declarator needs Box with an argument list, even though T has a default.

p08.why: int() is read as a function type, and a type is not valid for a constant parameter; the evidence says EDG reads the value 0 and accepts.

p09.why: Use<Kind> uses Kind's partial specialization for int*.

p10.why: A string literal copy-initializes a Text through its constructor.

p11.why: A pack takes the rest of the arguments, also none.

p12.why: The head has an int parameter and Long takes long; Clang 22 and GCC accept, Clang 18 and EDG reject.

p13.why: A placeholder type in either head matches any type in the other.

p14.why: 0.5 and 1.0 / 2 have one representation; 0.0 and -0.0 differ.

p15.why: The address of a member or an array element of a static object is valid.

p16.why: A floating-point value does not convert to int here.

p17.why: Local, incomplete and unnamed types are valid type arguments.

p18.why: In an explicit or partial specialization the injected class name names that specialization.

p19.why: A string literal is not valid for a pointer parameter.

p20.why: Lookup finds nothing or only a function, so pick<N> opens a list and argument-dependent lookup finds lib::pick; main returns 0.

p21.why: Derived* to Base* is a conversion to a base pointer, which is not allowed.

p22.why: Base alone is ambiguous between the injected names of Base<int> and Base<char>.

p23.why: Node alone names Node<int>, and Node<char> names another specialization.

p24.why: With T = int&, the later parameter T* is a pointer to a reference.

p25.why: Function, array of unknown bound, reference, const and closure types are valid type arguments.

p26.why: count is not a constant expression.

p27.why: The address of an automatic variable is not valid.

p28.why: int::size_type is not valid for the second parameter.

p30.why: An integer does not convert to a floating-point parameter.

p31.why: Both references name objects with static storage; fixed is constexpr so read gives 5, and counter reaches 2.

p32.why: The address of __func__ is not valid.

p33.why: A type is not valid for a constant parameter.

p34.why: Num takes a constant parameter and the head takes a type.

p35.why: >> closes two lists, and the operators in parentheses stay inside.

p36.why: Inside use, v is a variable so < is less-than; at namespace scope v names the template and v<1, 2> is 3.

p37.why: Box has one parameter and no pack.

p38.why: A scoped enumerator needs an explicit conversion to int.

p39.why: The integer 0 does not convert to a pointer here.

p40.why: The overloaded name pick selects the overload whose type the parameter has; main returns 0.

p41.why: The reference member would bind to a member of a temporary.

p42.why: identity has one parameter and the call gives two explicit arguments.

p43.why: The >> ends the list, and 2> does not fit after it.

p44.why: A union with no active member: Clang and EDG accept and give one specialization; GCC rejects the argument.

p45.why: int() is a function type, with no adjustment to a pointer.

p46.why: An alias template is a valid template template argument.

p48.why: Promotions, an unscoped enumerator and a constexpr user conversion keep the value, and 'a' and 97 are the same argument.

p49.why: A qualified name never finds the injected class name, so lib::Box needs arguments.

p50.why: Function and variable templates take explicit argument lists.

p51.why: Inside use, the parameter Size hides the template, so < and > are comparisons; outside, Size<3, 4> is a type.

p52.why: Defaults fill missing arguments and can use earlier parameters; <> takes all defaults.

p53.why: Arguments match parameters by position for each kind.

p54.why: A braced list copy-initializes the Point parameter, and equal members give the same specialization.

p55.why: Lookup finds nothing, so pick<5> opens a list and argument-dependent lookup at instantiation finds lib::pick.

p56.why: A variable template needs an argument list.

p58.why: Pair's extra parameter has a default, so it accepts the head's lists; the evidence says Clang 18 rejects.

p59.why: 5 would bind the reference to a temporary.

p60.why: Ref<a> and Ref<alias> refer to the same object, and &a and &b differ.

p61.why: Peek gets no access to Owner's private Hidden.

p63.why: Equal values and aliased types give the same specialization; const int and 3 give different ones.

p64.why: A variable template is not valid for a template template parameter.

p67.why: Clang treats ListAlias as its own template and passes; GCC and EDG treat it as List and the static_assert fails.

p68.why: An expression is not valid for a type parameter.

p69.why: Each pointer names a static object or function, also with internal linkage; address() reaches a static const int, which is usable in constant expressions.

p70.why: Pair's second parameter has no default, so it does not accept a one-argument list.

p71.why: int* to void* is not allowed.

p72.why: U has no argument and no default.

p73.why: Base is ambiguous also as a template template argument.

p74.why: Owner can name its own private Hidden in an argument.

p75.why: Named casts nest inside lists, and >> can close a list and a cast.

p76.why: The pack takes the rest, also none.

p77.why: A head with a pack accepts a template with any number of type parameters.

p78.why: On Clang ListAlias is its own template and the primary gives 0; on GCC and EDG it is List and the specialization gives 1, failing the assert.

p79.why: Owner::Hidden is private where the argument is written.

p80.why: Class parameters are copy-initialized from a value, a braced list or an int.

p81.why: As a template template argument, the injected class name names the template.

p82.why: A class is not valid for a template template parameter.

p83.why: Floating-point constants are valid for a double parameter.
